stories.headline: Amodei Meets Wiles and Bessent at White House in First Thaw Since Pentagon Blacklisting

key_facts.fact: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei met with White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday to discuss Mythos and potential collaboration.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined a meeting on Friday between White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, sources briefed on the meeting told Axios.

key_facts.fact: The White House called the meeting 'productive and constructive,' saying they discussed collaboration on cybersecurity, innovation, and AI safety.
key_facts.excerpt: The White House said the 'introductory meeting' with the company was 'both productive and constructive.' 'We discussed opportunities for collaboration, as well as shared approaches and protocols to address the challenges associated with scaling this technology.'

key_facts.fact: Both sides sought to wall off the Pentagon supply-chain-risk fight from how the rest of the government engages with Anthropic, with next steps focused on giving other departments access to Mythos.
key_facts.excerpt: Going into the meeting, both sides sought to wall off the Pentagon fight from the way the rest of the government engaged with Anthropic, and next steps are expected to be about how other departments engage with Anthropic's new Mythos Preview model.

key_facts.fact: Treasury and other agencies have expressed interest in joining the list of organizations with access to Mythos, and a deal could be struck soon.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury and other government agencies have expressed interest in joining that list. Two sources told Axios prior to the White House meeting that a deal along those lines could be struck soon.

key_facts.fact: When asked about the meeting, President Trump responded 'Who?' and said he had 'no idea' Amodei was there.
key_facts.excerpt: When President Donald Trump was asked about Amodei's visit on a runway in Phoenix, Ariz., he responded, 'Who?' and then said he had 'no idea.'

key_facts.fact: The meeting comes two months after Trump blacklisted Anthropic, calling it a 'radical left, woke company' and declaring 'we will not do business with them again.'

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Design, an AI Visual Tool That Sent Figma Stock Down 7%

key_facts.fact: Claude Design is an experimental product powered by Claude Opus 4.7 that lets users create prototypes, slides, wireframes, and one-pagers through conversational prompts.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic announced on Friday that it's launching Claude Design, a new experimental product that lets users create visuals like prototypes, slides, one-pagers, and more using Claude.

key_facts.fact: Claude Design is rolling out in research preview to Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscribers at no additional cost within existing limits.
key_facts.excerpt: Built on Claude Opus 4.7, the feature is available via the palette icon in the left-hand navigation panel of Claude.ai for Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscribers.

key_facts.fact: Usage of Claude Design is tracked separately from standard Claude chat and Claude Code limits, with individual weekly allowances.
key_facts.excerpt: Usage of Claude Design is tracked separately from the standard Claude chat and Claude Code limits. Subscribers have individual weekly allowances that sit alongside existing limits rather than replacing them.

key_facts.fact: The tool reads a team's codebase and design files during onboarding to extract design systems (colors, typography, components) and applies them automatically to every project.
key_facts.excerpt: During onboarding, Claude will read a team's codebase and design files to extract colors, typography, and components, then apply that system automatically to every subsequent project.

key_facts.fact: Designs can be exported as ZIP, PDF, or PPTX, sent to Canva, or handed off to Claude Code for implementation with a single instruction.
key_facts.excerpt: Designs can be sent to Canva, downloaded as PDF, PPTX, or standalone HTML, saved as a folder, or shared internally. When a design is ready to ship, Claude can bundle the design intent and assets into a package that can be passed to Claude Code.

stories.headline: FT: Anthropic Delays Wider Mythos Release Due to Compute Constraints, Not Just Safety

key_facts.fact: Multiple people with knowledge of Anthropic's operations told the FT the company is holding off from a wider Mythos release because it cannot reliably serve the model to customers, not primarily due to safety concerns.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has been limiting how widely its Mythos model is released, with sources pointing to reliability and capacity concerns as the driver. The reported issue is that Anthropic has suffered outages in recent weeks.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has suffered multiple outages in recent weeks, with March 2026 uptime dipping to 98.21% for Claude.ai, 98.32% for the API, and 98.56% for Claude Code.
key_facts.excerpt: March 2026 uptime dipped to 98.21% for Claude.ai, 98.32% for the API, and 98.56% for Claude Code. Anthropic's March 26–27 postmortem explicitly attributed elevated error rates on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 to 'networking performance degradation within our infrastructure.'

key_facts.fact: The reliability issues are shaping the Mythos rollout timeline: Anthropic is waiting until it can maintain consistent throughput before expanding distribution beyond initial Project Glasswing partners.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is waiting until it can 'reliably serve' Mythos to customers before expanding distribution. Rollout timing may depend on operational readiness rather than raw model availability.

key_facts.fact: Meanwhile, Opus 4.7 users are reporting the new tokenizer increases token consumption by about 30%, which burns through rate limits faster and raises costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Opus 4.7 can also use up a whole lot more tokens. The model has a new tokenizer, which means that one input can cost significantly more.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic increased subscriber rate limits to compensate for the higher token burn, but critics on Reddit and X called Opus 4.7 a 'serious regression' in some use cases.
key_facts.excerpt: Cherny later announced that Anthropic was increasing 'subscriber rate limits to make up for it.' One Reddit post titled, 'Claude Opus 4.7 is a serious regression, not an upgrade,' has 2,300 upvotes.

stories.headline: China Launches First Satellite Combining Active and Passive Greenhouse Gas Monitoring

key_facts.fact: China claims two world firsts: the first combined active and passive monitoring of greenhouse gases, and the first imaging system to synchronously observe both nadir and limb directions for 3D atmospheric monitoring.

key_facts.fact: The satellite orbits at about 700 kilometers in a sun-synchronous orbit; the launch marks the 638th flight of the Long March carrier rocket series.

stories.headline: EU Awards €180M Sovereign Cloud Contract to Four European Providers to Cut US Tech Dependence

key_facts.fact: The European Commission awarded a six-year, €180 million ($212 million) sovereign cloud tender to four European provider groups: Luxembourg's Post Telecom, Germany's StackIT, Iliad's Scaleway, and Belgium's Proximus.
key_facts.excerpt: The tender, launched in October 2025, was awarded to Luxembourg's Post Telecom, Germany's StackIT, French Iliad's data centre unit Scaleway and Belgium's Proximus.

key_facts.fact: The Proximus consortium includes Mistral AI, Clarence, and S3NS — a joint venture between Thales and Google Cloud — meaning one sovereign cloud contract will run on US-origin technology under European governance.
key_facts.excerpt: Proximus, partnering with S3NS – a joint venture between French defence and technology group Thales and Google Cloud, alongside Clarence and Mistral AI.

key_facts.fact: The Commission stated that 'non-European technologies, when operated within a strict and appropriate framework, can meet the minimum level of sovereignty required' — a significant policy statement drawing a line between sovereign operation and sovereign technology.
key_facts.excerpt: The Commission addressed this directly in its announcement, stating that 'non-European technologies, when operated within a strict and appropriate framework, can meet the minimum level of sovereignty required.'

key_facts.fact: Post Telecom is partnering with OVHcloud and CleverCloud; OVHcloud shares rose ~2.5% on the news. OVHcloud's CEO said the consortium was selected to provide cloud for the Commission's 40+ agencies.
key_facts.excerpt: Post Telecom is bringing on partners OVHcloud and CleverCloud... OVHcloud founder and CEO Octave Klaba said the Post Telecom consortium had been selected to provide cloud services for the European Commission's more than 40 agencies.

key_facts.fact: EU digital chief Henna Virkkunen said on X: 'Scaling the use of EU cloud is key to strengthening Europe's digital sovereignty.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Scaling the use of EU cloud is key to strengthening Europe's digital sovereignty,' Henna Virkkunen, the EU's digital chief, said on X.

stories.headline: Oil Drops 9% and S&P 500 Hits Record as Iran Reopens Strait of Hormuz Under Shaky Ceasefire

key_facts.fact: Brent crude fell 9.1% to settle at $90.38 per barrel, and US WTI dropped 9.4% to $82.59, though both remain above the pre-war $70 level.

key_facts.fact: Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Ghalibaf dismissed Trump's claims on X: 'The President of the United States made seven claims in one hour, all seven of which were false,' adding the Strait 'will not remain open' if the US blockade continues.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The President of the United States made seven claims in one hour, all seven of which were false,' chief Iranian negotiator Mohammad Ghalibaf wrote on X late Friday.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said 21 ships had been turned back to Iran since the blockade began on Monday; the US Navy's blockade of Iranian ports remains 'in full force.'
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. forces have sent 21 ships back to Iran since the blockade began on Monday, U.S. Central Command said on X.

key_facts.excerpt: A data firm, Kpler, said movement through the strait remained confined to corridors requiring Iran's approval.

key_facts.fact: On Saturday April 18, Iranian state TV cited the Armed Forces spokesperson saying the Strait of Hormuz 'has returned to its previous state' under strict military control, reversing Friday's reopening announcement so long as the US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in force.

stories.headline: Kairos Power Breaks Ground on Hermes 2, First Gen IV Nuclear Reactor With US Construction Permit

key_facts.fact: Kairos Power broke ground on April 17 on the Hermes 2 Demonstration Plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee — the first commercial-scale Gen IV reactor to receive a US construction permit
key_facts.excerpt: Kairos Power broke ground on the Hermes 2 Demonstration Plant in Oak Ridge on Friday. It is the first commercial-scale reactor and the first power-producing Generation IV reactor to receive a U.S. construction permit.

key_facts.fact: The reactor uses molten fluoride salt coolant with specialty fuel, building on technology rooted in Oak Ridge's 1960s Molten Salt Reactor Experiment
key_facts.excerpt: The Hermes reactor design uses molten fluoride salt coolant along with a specialty fuel to generate power.

key_facts.fact: Once completed, the plant is expected to generate up to 50 megawatts for the TVA power system, powering Google's data centers in Tennessee and Alabama
key_facts.excerpt: Once completed, the plant is expected to generate up to 50 megawatts for the TVA power system, powering Google's data centers in Tennessee and Alabama.

key_facts.fact: TVA expects the first reactor at Hermes 2 to begin operating in 2030, with further capacity by 2035; TVA is the first US utility to buy electricity from a Gen IV reactor
key_facts.excerpt: The TVA expects one reactor at Hermes 2 to begin operating in 2030, with the company adding further capacity by 2035. The TVA is the first U.S. utility to sign an agreement to buy electricity from a Gen IV reactor.

key_facts.fact: The plant is built on the former Oak Ridge Gaseous Diffusion Plant K-33 site, next to the Hermes 1 test reactor (expected operational 2028)
key_facts.excerpt: Leaders with Kairos Power broke ground on Hermes 2, a fluoride salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor designed to produce electricity. The company said the project builds on lessons from Hermes 1, which is already under construction and serving as a test reactor.

key_facts.fact: Deputy Secretary of Energy James Danly attended the groundbreaking, saying the DOE is 'partnering with all manner of different companies to get as much nuclear power development as possible'
key_facts.excerpt: The Department of Energy, under the president's mandate to accelerate nuclear power, has been, partnering with all manner of different companies to get as much nuclear power development as possible, as quickly as possible.

stories.headline: Meta Targets May 20 for First Wave of ~8,000 Layoffs as AI Spending Reshapes Workforce

key_facts.fact: Meta plans to execute the first wave of layoffs on May 20, cutting approximately 8,000 employees — roughly 10% of its global workforce of ~79,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta plans to execute the first wave of what could be its most sweeping round of layoffs ever—close to 8,000 employees, or roughly 10% of its global workforce, gone in a single cut.

key_facts.fact: A second wave of layoffs is planned for the second half of 2026, though details on timing, scale, and scope have not been finalized.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is planning more cuts in the second half, though details including date and size have not been defined. Executives may adjust their plans as they observe developments in artificial intelligence capabilities.

key_facts.fact: Roles in sales, recruiting, middle management, and non-AI-adjacent functions are considered most at risk; engineers are being moved into a new 'Applied AI' organization focused on autonomous AI agents.
key_facts.excerpt: Roles in sales, recruiting, middle management, and non-AI-adjacent functions considered most at risk... engineers from across the company have been moved into a new 'Applied AI' organisation focused on building autonomous AI agents.

key_facts.fact: Meta has committed up to $135 billion in capital expenditure in 2026 alone and $600 billion toward US AI infrastructure by 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has committed up to $135 billion in capital expenditure this year alone and $600 billion toward US AI infrastructure by 2028.

key_facts.fact: These will be Meta's largest layoffs since the 2022-2023 'year of efficiency' restructuring that eliminated about 21,000 workers.
key_facts.excerpt: As demissões em massa da Meta este ano serão as mais significativas da gigante da mídia social desde uma reestruturação no final de 2022 e início de 2023 que ela apelidou de 'ano da eficiência', quando eliminou cerca de 21 mil trabalhadores.

stories.headline: OpenAI Loses Three Executives as It Sheds 'Side Quests' to Focus on Enterprise AI

key_facts.fact: Kevin Weil (VP of AI for Science, former CPO), Bill Peebles (Sora team lead), and Srinivas Narayanan (CTO of B2B Applications) all announced their departures on Friday.
key_facts.excerpt: Kevin Weil, who led the company's science research initiative, and Bill Peebles, the researcher behind AI video tool Sora, both announced their departures on Friday.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is shuttering Prism, the AI workspace for scientists Weil headed, and folding its capabilities into the Codex desktop app.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's Prism, a recently-announced research-focused 'workspace for scientists' that Weil was heading up, is being sunsetted, and OpenAI's plan is to fold its capabilities into the Codex desktop app, according to Wired.

key_facts.fact: The departures follow OpenAI shutting down Sora last month, which was losing an estimated $1 million per day in compute costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Sora, which was losing an estimated $1 million per day in compute costs, was shut down last month.

key_facts.fact: Weil's departure came one day after his team released GPT-Rosalind, a new model for life sciences and drug discovery.
key_facts.excerpt: Weil's departure comes a day after his team released GPT-Rosalind, a new model to accelerate life sciences research and drug discovery.

key_facts.fact: The exits come weeks after product and business chief Fidji Simo took medical leave, marketing chief Kate Rouch stepped down, and COO Brad Lightcap moved to 'special projects.'
key_facts.excerpt: Their exits come just weeks after Fidji Simo, OpenAI's product and business chief, announced she would take a medical leave. Kate Rouch, OpenAI's marketing chief, also decided to step down to focus on her cancer recovery earlier this month, and Brad Lightcap, OpenAI's operating chief, transitioned to a new role focused on 'special projects.'

stories.headline: Four-Month-Old Recursive Superintelligence Raises $500M+ at $4B Valuation From GV and Nvidia

key_facts.fact: Recursive Superintelligence has raised at least $500 million in a round led by Google's venture arm GV with backing from Nvidia, valuing the company at $4 billion pre-money.
key_facts.excerpt: Recursive Superintelligence, the four-month-old AI startup founded by former Salesforce chief scientist Richard Socher, has raised at least $500 million in a round led by Google's venture arm GV with backing from chipmaker Nvidia.

key_facts.fact: The round was so oversubscribed it could eventually reach $1 billion, according to people familiar with the deal.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing values the London-incorporated company at $4 billion before new capital and was so oversubscribed it could eventually reach $1 billion.

key_facts.fact: The London-incorporated company was founded by former Salesforce chief scientist Richard Socher, DeepMind director Tim Rocktäschel, and ex-OpenAI researchers Josh Tobin, Jeff Clune, and Tim Shi, with about 20 people on staff.
key_facts.excerpt: Tim Rocktäschel holds an AI professorship at University College London and until recently ran Google DeepMind's Open-Endedness group... Former OpenAI researchers Josh Tobin, Jeff Clune, and Tim Shi round out the publicly identified lineup... About 20 people work there.

key_facts.fact: The company aims to automate the entire AI development pipeline — from evaluation and data selection through training, post-training, and research direction.
key_facts.excerpt: Asked which slice of frontier AI development Recursive wants to automate, whether evaluation, data selection, training, post-training, or research direction itself, Socher answered: 'Option C, all of the above.'

stories.headline: Recursive Superintelligence Raises $500M+ at $4B Valuation for Self-Teaching AI

key_facts.fact: Recursive Superintelligence, a four-month-old startup, raised at least $500M in a round led by Google's venture arm GV with backing from Nvidia, at a $4B pre-money valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Recursive Superintelligence, the four-month-old AI startup founded by former Salesforce chief scientist Richard Socher, has raised at least $500 million in a round led by Google's venture arm GV with backing from chipmaker Nvidia. The financing values the London-incorporated company at $4 billion before new capital.

key_facts.fact: The round was so oversubscribed it could eventually reach $1 billion, according to people familiar with the deal.
key_facts.excerpt: The round was so oversubscribed it could eventually reach $1 billion, people familiar with the deal told the FT.

key_facts.fact: Co-founders include Richard Socher (ex-Salesforce chief scientist), Tim Rocktäschel (UCL professor, ex-DeepMind director), and former OpenAI researchers Josh Tobin, Jeff Clune, and Tim Shi.
key_facts.excerpt: The FT named Recursive's core founders for the first time. Alongside Socher: Tim Rocktäschel, Berlin-born UCL professor and until recently director and principal scientist at Google DeepMind's Open-Endedness group. Former OpenAI researchers Josh Tobin, Jeff Clune, and Tim Shi round out the publicly identified lineup.

key_facts.fact: The company aims to automate the entire AI development pipeline — from evaluation through research direction — and has about 20 employees.
key_facts.excerpt: Asked which slice of frontier AI development Recursive wants to automate, whether evaluation, data selection, training, post-training, or research direction itself, Socher answered: 'Option C, all of the above.' About 20 people work there.

key_facts.fact: The public launch is expected around mid-May 2026, when the technical claims about self-improving AI will face their first real test.
key_facts.excerpt: The public launch is expected in May, Socher told Implicator.ai, and that is when the technical claims about self-improving AI meet the first real test.

key_facts.excerpt: US tech companies successfully lobbied the EU to hide data centers' environmental toll.

key_facts.fact: One of the corporate demands was written 'almost verbatim' into EU rules governing data center emissions reporting
key_facts.excerpt: One of their demands was written almost verbatim into EU rules.

key_facts.fact: The lobbying effort targeted EU rules that would have required greater transparency about the environmental impact of the rapidly expanding data center industry
